the composite NF‐AT/AP‐1 element (− 115 to − 80) is crucial for IL‐5 synthesis in human peripheral T lymphocytes.

the transcriptional regulation of the human IL-5 gene in peripheral blood lymphocytes from asthmatic patients.
the transcriptional regulation of the human IL-5 gene in peripheral blood lymphocytes.

IL‐5 production by human peripheral T cells is mediated by a composite NFAT/AP-1 binding site located at the IL-5 promoter region, and the transcriptional regulation of the gene is dependent on both NFAT/AP- 1 binding activity and T cell activation.

the IL‐5 promoter is a complex structure that contains multiple cis‐regulatory elements, and that the composite NF‐AT/AP‐1 element plays a crucial role as a master switch in the transcriptional regulation of the human IL5 gene in peripheral blood T cells.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the composite NF‐AT/AP‐1‐binding element (− 114 to − 101) plays a crucial function in IL‐5 manufacturing by peripheral T cells from asthmatic sufferers.
the IL‐5 production by T cells of astmatics is regulated by a composite cis‐regulatory site (− 115to− 100) composed of NFAT and AP‐1 binding sites.
IL‐5 production by peripheral T cells in asthmatic patients is regulated at the level of transcription by a composite binding site for NFAT/AP‐I.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IL‐5 gene regulation is mediated by the composite NFAT‐AP‐1 site in the promoter/enhancer region.
the composite NF‐AT/AP‐1 element plays a crucial role for IL‐5 synthesis in human T cells of asthmatc patients.
the IL‐5 promoter is regulated in a cell‐type‐specific manner, and the mechanism of IL‐5 regulation differs between Th1 and Th2 cells.
